note: Separate slimming measurements on Qwen3.5-9B, written 2026-10-29 before any run. Corpus, expert sets and learned routers come from moe_carve_rules_v2.json. Every KL is from the stock dense model on the same tokens.

predictions.vocab: Domain-equal bits per byte rise by less than 2% with the 64K vocabulary; science and biomed change most.
predictions.cache: With 16,384 rows the model's own top pick is outside the cache at under 5% of eval positions, and the detector falls back on under 25% of positions at 95% recall of those misses. 4,096 rows misses the top pick at least twice as often.
predictions.state: int16_row and fp16_sr stay within 3x of fp32_jitter's KL from stock; bf16 is at least 10x fp32_jitter's; int8_row is worse than bf16.
predictions.generate: int16_row and fp16_sr answers finish within 10% of fp32's mean length; bf16 differs by more.
predictions.deltanet: Dropping the 4 least important DeltaNet blocks costs under 0.3 nats; 8 costs more than twice as much. Low rank at the same parameter saving is worse than dropping blocks.
predictions.combined: The combined body's KL is within 30% of the sum of the separate KLs (learned router, int16 state, chosen DeltaNet cut). The 16K cache with its detector lowers greedy agreement with the dense model by under 2 points.

criteria.cheap: A step is cheap if it costs under 0.05 nats of domain-equal KL (under 1% bits per byte for the vocabulary) and its copy-span p99 KL is no more than 25% above its reference's.
criteria.detector: The detector's threshold keeps 95% recall of top-pick misses on calibration positions; eval recall is reported, not tuned.
